Library of Congress puts Krishnaraja Wodeyar III's 1856 board games book online

An illustrated printed book on board games attributed to the Mysore ruler Krishnaraja Wodeyar III can now be viewed and downloaded free from the Library of Congress. Its text is in Telugu, Kannada and Sanskrit, written in Telugu script.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 25 November 2026

Where
Online (Library of Congress, Washington)

The Library of Congress has made a mid-19th-century book on board games, catalogued under the name of Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, Maharaja of Mysore, openly available online after scanning its copy. Jonathan Loar, South Asia reference specialist in the library's Asian Division, announced the release on the INDOLOGY mailing list on 23 November 2026 and said the scan was a one-off project.

The library's catalogue record dates the book to 1856 (given in the imprint as 1778) and names the Vartamānataraṅgiṇī press as printer, in Cennapaṭṭaṇa, a place the cataloguers supplied in square brackets. It runs to 72, 4, 3 and 8 pages with colour illustrations, is 28 cm tall and has an index. The catalogue says the text mixes type with handwriting, and that it is in Telugu, Kannada and Sanskrit, all written in Telugu script.

The long title, transliterated in the record, includes the words Caturaṅga sārasarvasva, and the library files the book under board games of the princely state of Mysore, their rules and pictures. Loar's post says it covers both board games and game theory. The catalogue sums it up as a "rare mid-19th century illustrated printed work on board games".

The front flyleaf carries a blind stamp in English naming the Maharaja of Mysore, and the name Kṛṣṇabhūpati in Kannada script. The record does not say how the copy reached Washington. Krishnaraja Wodeyar III is catalogued as active from 1799 to 1868.

The scans can be read page by page or downloaded as a single PDF, and the book has been added to the library's South Asian Digital Collection. According to the library, items in that collection are out of copyright or carry no known restrictions, so anyone may reuse them, crediting the Library of Congress, Asian Division.

Sources

  1. Śrīkṛṣṇabhūvarakṛtasaṅkhyā ratnasphuranamaḥ ... Caturaṅga sārasarvasva (catalogue record and digitised copy), Library of Congress, 2026-11-25
  2. Newly digitized: 19th c. board games and game theory work by Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, INDOLOGY mailing list, 2026-11-23
